# Cached stacked-column controls

These twelve original DOCX controls are generated by
`tools/stacked_charts_fixture.py` from the project's original chart/anchor OPC
shell. The caches, colors, dimensions and chart settings are authored directly
with lxml; no engine export or corpus content supplies the reference input.
The reference application exported each PDF without saving the source document.
The auxiliary variants' complete OPC contents were compared with their reference
input packages. `record_stacked_charts.py` records package/PDF hashes, axis tick
strings and rectangles extracted from native PDF paths.

The controls cover ordinary stacking, percentage stacking, positive/negative
and mixed signs, an empty category, an entirely zero-valued chart, inversion
disabled, no-fill negative series, explicit negative outlines, and omitted,
zero, positive and negative overlap. XML cache points are deliberately in
reverse index order. The reference application normalizes percentages using each category's total
absolute values, then accumulates positive and negative segments separately.
All-zero categories draw no bars. A zero-only percentage chart has a 0–100%
axis. Omitted overlap equals zero; explicit 100% aligns the stack horizontally.

The reference application inverts negative filled segments to white by default, with a black
outline when none is supplied. It preserves an explicit outline color and
does not invent a fill or outline for a no-fill/no-outline series. Explicit
`invertIfNegative="0"` retains the series colors. This refines behavior not
fully specified by the short inversion description in §21.2.2.86; it is not
a claimed contradiction of an explicit RGB inversion formula.

Tests compare bar and outline positions normalized to the plot rectangle
within 0.001 of the plot dimensions, colors exactly, and tick strings exactly.
The bound covers the reference application's subpoint PDF coordinate rounding. Browser tests also
sample actual canvas pixels and exercise no-edit package equality, text edits,
unrelated-part preservation, exact undo and reopening. Existing clustered
chart regression tests remain in place; their old unsupported-grouping example
now uses the still-unsupported depth-axis `standard` grouping.

These are **not** full chart-layout equivalence tests against the native reference. Chart font choice,
absolute plot margins and label layout still use the existing preview policy.
The quarterly-report chart additionally requires theme/metadata/text-format
support and remains unsupported by strict import. No fallback image replaces
chart data in saved DOCX packages.
